title: Start the pinned Rauthy against a scratch PostgreSQL in a demand gate leg and pass only when it answers ready
blocked_by: DIRECTORY-002 has landed and records the two members R1 reads: a stranger checks it with git cat-file -e origin/main:deploy/identity/versions.json, which exits 0 only once the file is on main, and then with `git show origin/main:deploy/identity/versions.json | python3 -c "import json,re,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ok=isinstance(d,dict) and isinstance(d.get('rauthy_image_id'),str) and isinstance(d.get('postgres_image'),str) and re.fullmatch(r'sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}',d['rauthy_image_id']) is not None and re.fullmatch(r'[^@\s]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}',d['postgres_image']) is not None; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"`, which exits 0 only when that file is a JSON object whose rauthy_image_id matches sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters and whose postgres_image matches <repository>@sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. This brief reads that file and duplicates neither value.

An image built from ablative-io/rauthy at the vendor/rauthy pin exists at the venue, and that build itself set its org.opencontainers.image.revision label to the pin commit. deploy/identity/versions.json records that image by its local image ID, the sha256 content ID that docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' prints, beside the pinned revision, and never as <repo>@sha256:<digest>; no registry is involved and the image is never pushed or pulled. A stranger checks it with docker image inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}}' on the Rauthy image ID in versions.json, which prints the output of git rev-parse HEAD:vendor/rauthy only once that image is in place. Measured at main 7b53625: the pin is dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662, and the upstream ghcr.io/sebadob/rauthy:0.36.2 image (sha256:f7d3c501402165e023edbd958b032b41c9cfdac5ea7f8ca7d62217327145577e) carries no org.opencontainers.image.revision label, so R1 refuses it as rauthy_revision_mismatch. A label written onto an image not built from the pin is refused as a source, and there is no fallback. Building the image is venue work outside this brief.
purpose: DIRECTORY-002 will install the maintained Rauthy, SpiceDB and one PostgreSQL database, but no gate leg starts the Rauthy container and checks it, and the release row holds that gap as a blocker. This brief adds one gate leg, cadence demand, to the lys design project file and to the directory cluster's gate. The leg starts the Rauthy pinned in vendor/rauthy in a container against a scratch PostgreSQL container, waits for Rauthy's readiness answer, then stops and removes everything it made. It passes only on that answer, refuses by name when the runtime or an image is missing, and lets no secret into its output. A test run by a round leg proves the last of these by searching the output for every secret value the runtime received.
task: Write the leg's command as one standard-library Python script at scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py (R1). Write a Rust integration test at crates/lys/tests/rauthy_ready_leg.rs that runs the script against a stub container runtime and counts what fired (R2). Append the leg to docs/design/project.json (R3) and to the directory cluster's design.json gate (R4). How a person asks for the leg until the method can: from the repository root on the venue, run `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py`. The request path inside the method's ledger is design-system card 9jJgCzeG and is out of scope here. That card also carries the acceptance line that a round records rauthy-ready as Unmeasured, with a reason containing 'requires tool:docker', on a venue declaring no tool:docker. This brief does not claim that line, and it lands without it. In scope: the one script, the one test file, one appended leg in each of the two design files, and the directory cluster's rendered markdown that render-cluster.py rewrites from the amended design.json. Out of scope: .land/gates.sh, which is not changed; every existing leg; any round-cadence leg; SpiceDB; building or pulling any image; moving the vendor/rauthy pin; any file under deploy/identity/, which is DIRECTORY-002's and is read, never written. The script is a check, not a provisioning engine: it installs nothing durable, and every object it creates is removed before it exits. That keeps it clear of DIRECTORY-002's boundary against a Python or shell provisioning engine. It reads the image references DIRECTORY-002 records and provisions nothing that DIRECTORY-002's lys identity subcommands own.

requirements.title: Start the pinned Rauthy against a scratch PostgreSQL container, pass only on its ready answer, and remove everything the leg made
requirements.spec: WHEN python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL do the following, in order. The versions file is deploy/identity/versions.json under the repository the script lives in, unless the one optional argument --versions-file <path> names another file, which is then read instead; the script takes no other argument. (1) Read the vendor/rauthy pin as the commit git rev-parse HEAD:vendor/rauthy prints in the repository the script lives in; the submodule need not be initialised. (2) Read from the versions file, a JSON object, two top-level string members: rauthy_image_id, the Rauthy image's local image ID (sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, as docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' prints it), and postgres_image, the PostgreSQL image's digest reference (<repository>@sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters). DIRECTORY-002's R1 records image digests in deploy/identity/versions.json but names no members for them, so DIRECTORY-002 must record these two under exactly these names. (3) Check that the container runtime answers: the docker client is on PATH and docker version reaches its daemon. (4) Check that each image is present locally with docker image inspect: first the Rauthy image ID, and only when that succeeds, the PostgreSQL digest reference. (5) Read the Rauthy image's org.opencontainers.image.revision label and compare it with the pin. (6) Create one network, one PostgreSQL container and one Rauthy container. Each carries the name lys-rauthy-ready-<run>-<role>, where <run> is a random hexadecimal identifier drawn for that run, and the label io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready=<run>. The PostgreSQL container publishes no host port. The Rauthy container publishes its HTTP port only on 127.0.0.1, with a host port the runtime picks. Every docker run carries --pull never. (7) Wait until docker exec pg_isready succeeds in the PostgreSQL container. (8) Read the Rauthy container's published port with docker port and poll http://127.0.0.1:<that port>/auth/v1/health. The Rauthy container is started with HEALTH_CHECK_DELAY_SECS=0, so the early answer Rauthy gives inside that delay cannot count. (9) Pass only when that endpoint answers HTTP 200 with a JSON body whose db_healthy and cache_healthy are both true, printing one line beginning 'ready:' to stdout and exiting 0. (10) On every exit path, pass, refusal, failure or interruption by SIGINT or SIGTERM, stop and remove each container with its anonymous volumes, then the network, then the private temporary directory. The removal goes by the exact names this run created. The leg generates five secret values from Python's secrets module and hands them to the runtime only through --env-file files created with mode 0600 in that temporary directory. The five are the PostgreSQL password (POSTGRES_PASSWORD for PostgreSQL, PG_PASSWORD for Rauthy), ENC_KEYS, BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_PLAIN, HQL_SECRET_RAFT and HQL_SECRET_API. IF the docker client is absent from PATH, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as container_runtime_missing, and it SHALL do the same when docker version cannot reach the daemon. IF docker image inspect of the Rauthy image ID fails, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as image_missing. The refusal names rauthy, that image ID and the pin it was built from, then the one command that produces an image carrying that pin, `docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=<pin> --load .`, run in the Rauthy source checked out at the pin, with <pin> written out as the pin commit, followed by the check that reads the ID back, `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' <image ID>`, with <image ID> written out. That refusal SHALL NOT contain the word 'pull'. IF the PostgreSQL image is not present locally, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as image_missing, naming postgres and the digest reference, and SHALL tell the operator to pull that digest reference before running. IF the revision label is absent, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as rauthy_revision_mismatch. The refusal says the image carries no revision label, contains the word 'absent', names the pin, and names the build command that makes a labelled image: `docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=<pin> --load .`, run in the Rauthy source checked out at the pin, with <pin> written out as the pin commit. IF the revision label differs from the pin, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as rauthy_revision_mismatch, naming the label's value and the pin. IF git cannot read the pin, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as rauthy_pin_unreadable. IF the versions file is absent or is not a JSON object, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as versions_unreadable, naming the file's path. IF rauthy_image_id or postgres_image is missing, is not a string, or does not have the form step (2) gives it, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as versions_unreadable, naming the file's path and each such member. That check (2) runs before check (3), so it needs no container runtime. IF pg_isready has not succeeded within 60 seconds, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as readiness_timeout, naming postgres and the bound. IF Rauthy has not answered ready within 60 seconds, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as readiness_timeout, naming rauthy and the bound. IF a runtime command the leg issues exits non-zero, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse as runtime_step_failed, naming the step and the exit status. Every refusal is one line on stderr of the form 'refused: <name>: <detail>' and exits 1. All checks (1) to (5) complete before anything is created, so a refusal among them creates nothing. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT pull, build, tag or relabel an image, SHALL NOT refer to the Rauthy image by a <repo>@sha256:<digest> reference, and it SHALL NOT accept an image with no revision label on any other evidence. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT exit 0 on any path except the ready answer, and it SHALL NOT report a missing prerequisite as a skip. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT probe a fixed port or any port read from another container. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT stop, remove, or connect to any container, network or volume it did not create in this run. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT print a secret value, container logs, docker inspect output of a container, the runtime's own stdout or stderr, or the contents of an env file. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT pass a secret value on a command line. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT start SpiceDB, and it SHALL NOT write any file outside its private temporary directory. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write the versions file, and SHALL NOT fall back to deploy/identity/versions.json when --versions-file names a file that cannot be read.
acceptance: On a venue with docker, the image named by rauthy_image_id and the image named by postgres_image in deploy/identity/versions.json present locally, and the Rauthy image's org.opencontainers.image.revision label equal to git rev-parse HEAD:vendor/rauthy, running `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py` from the repository root exits 0 and prints exactly one stdout line beginning 'ready:'.

On that venue, `docker ps -aq --filter label=io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready` prints 0 lines after the passing run, and `docker network ls -q --filter label=io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready` prints 0 lines after the passing run.
On that venue, `docker volume ls -q | wc -l` prints the same number before and after the passing run.
On that venue, `docker ps -a --format '{{.ID}} {{.State}} {{.Label "io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready"}}'` lines whose label field is empty are identical before and after the passing run.

On a machine whose PATH holds python3 and git but no docker, running `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py` from the repository root exits 1, prints no 'ready:' line, and prints to stderr a line beginning 'refused: container_runtime_missing'.

With the vendor/rauthy pin at dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662, running `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py --versions-file <f>` from the repository root on that venue, where <f> is a file written for this measurement holding a JSON object whose rauthy_image_id is the local image ID of an image present on the venue that carries no org.opencontainers.image.revision label, such as the upstream ghcr.io/sebadob/rauthy:0.36.2 image, and whose postgres_image is a digest reference present on the venue, exits 1 with a stderr line beginning 'refused: rauthy_revision_mismatch'. That line contains 'absent', contains dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662, and contains 'docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662'. Afterwards `docker ps -aq --filter label=io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready` prints 0 lines. `git status --porcelain -- deploy/identity` prints the same lines before and after the run.

With the vendor/rauthy pin at dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662, running `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py --versions-file <f>` from the repository root on that venue, where <f> is a file written for this measurement holding a JSON object whose rauthy_image_id is sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters naming no image present on the venue, and whose postgres_image is a digest reference present on the venue, exits 1 with a stderr line beginning 'refused: image_missing'. That line contains 'rauthy', that image ID, 'docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662 --load .' and "docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}'", and it contains 'pull' 0 times. Afterwards `docker ps -aq --filter label=io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready` prints 0 lines. `git status --porcelain -- deploy/identity` prints the same lines before and after the run.
On that venue, `docker image ls -q --no-trunc | sort` prints identical lines before and after the passing run.

On any machine with python3 and git, with or without docker, running `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py --versions-file <f>` from the repository root, where <f> holds a JSON object with postgres_image set to a digest reference and no rauthy_image_id member, exits 1, prints no 'ready:' line, and prints to stderr a line beginning 'refused: versions_unreadable' that contains <f> and 'rauthy_image_id' and does not contain 'postgres_image'.

On any machine with python3 and git, running the same command with <f> naming a path that does not exist exits 1 with a stderr line beginning 'refused: versions_unreadable' that contains <f>, and `git status --porcelain -- deploy/identity` prints the same lines before and after the run.

With the vendor/rauthy pin at dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662 and --versions-file <f>, where <f> holds a JSON object whose rauthy_image_id is sha256: followed by 64 zeros, an ID naming no image on the venue, and whose postgres_image is a digest reference present on the venue, the run exits 1 with a stderr line beginning 'refused: image_missing' that contains sha256: followed by 64 zeros; the ID read came from <f>, not from deploy/identity/versions.json.

files_changed.note: The rauthy-ready leg. It reads the pin and the versions file (checks 1 and 2), checks the runtime (3), both images (4) and the Rauthy revision label (5) before creating anything. It then creates a network and the PostgreSQL and Rauthy containers under lys-rauthy-ready-<run>-<role> with the io.lys.gate.rauthy-ready=<run> label and --pull never, waits for pg_isready and polls /auth/v1/health on the port docker port reports on 127.0.0.1. It prints 'ready:' only on 200 with both flags true and removes everything it made on every exit path.

The line is printed after cleanup succeeds. Met in code; it can only be measured at the venue, which I did not do. Row 2 (0 labelled containers and networks afterwards): Run.cleanup (:294) runs in main's finally. It stops each container, runs rm --volumes on it, then network rm, then rmtree on the temp directory, all by the exact names recorded in Run.containers and Run.network. Run.start (:279) records a name before its docker run, so a container a failed run left behind is still found by name (container inspect) and removed. Row 3 (volume count unchanged): containers are removed with rm --volumes (:323) and the script creates no named volume. Row 4 (containers without the label unchanged): nothing is stopped or removed except names this run created (:310-325). Row 5 (no docker on PATH): check_runtime (:183) uses shutil.which('docker') and refuses 'container_runtime_missing'. A non-zero docker version gives the same refusal. Row 6 (label absent): check_images (:195) reads the labels as '{{json .Config.Labels}}' from the image, never a container, and never prints them. A missing or empty label gives 'refused: rauthy_revision_mismatch' containing 'absent', the pin and `docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=<pin> --load .` (:227-234). This runs before anything is created. Row 7 (Rauthy image missing): the image_missing refusal (:199-208) names rauthy, the image ID, the pin, the build command ending ' --load .' and `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' <id>`. It contains no 'pull'. Row 8 (image list unchanged): the script never pulls, builds, tags or relabels, and every run carries --pull never (:282). Row 9 (rauthy_image_id missing): read_versions (:131) names the path and each bad member only. With only rauthy_image_id bad, 'postgres_image' does not appear. It runs before check_runtime, so it needs no docker. Row 10 (versions path does not exist): OSError gives 'refused: versions_unreadable' with the path. There is no fallback to the default file. Row 11 (image ID of 64 zeros): the ID comes only from the --versions-file path parse_arguments (:91) returns. The image_missing line contains that ID. Other points: the five secrets are drawn in draw_secrets (:339) and written only to 0600 O_EXCL env files (:244). Runtime stdout is captured and never printed, and stderr goes to DEVNULL (:157). The probe uses ProxyHandler({}) so it reaches only 127.0.0.1 (:403). The 60-second bounds are at :56, :352 and :400. SIGINT and SIGTERM raise Interrupted so cleanup runs (:461, :493). Nothing is written outside mkdtemp, and deploy/identity is only read. The venue rows (1 to 4, 6, 7, 8 and 11) need a docker venue and are not measured here.
dev.deviation: Four deviations from the brief. (a) Order: step (6) lists creating the network, PostgreSQL and Rauthy containers before step (7), the pg_isready wait. The script starts Rauthy only after pg_isready succeeds (start_and_probe, :418), because a Rauthy that starts before its database accepts TCP connections may exit and turn a healthy install into a readiness_timeout. The Rauthy 60-second bound starts from its own start. (b) Two refusal names the brief does not list: 'arguments_invalid' for any argument other than one --versions-file <path>, and 'interrupted' for SIGINT or SIGTERM. Both print one 'refused:' line and exit 1 after cleanup. (c) The brief's 60-second readiness bounds, and a per-request urllib timeout capped at the remaining bound, conflict with CLAUDE.md's 'No time limits' rule. I followed the brief because its refusal rows and the never-ready test depend on the bound; the conflict needs a ruling. (d) The postgres image_missing refusal says 'pull it before running: docker pull <ref>'. The brief requires telling the operator to pull; the leg itself never pulls.

requirements.title: Run the leg against a stub runtime in a round-leg test, counting refusals, cleanup, the probe and every secret it searched for
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL add the Rust integration test crates/lys/tests/rauthy_ready_leg.rs, run by the tests leg (cargo test --workspace --all-features), which runs `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py` as a child process from the repository root. PATH starts with a temporary directory holding a stub docker executable that the test writes. The stub appends every argv it receives to a record file. When it receives --env-file, it copies that file's contents into the record, so the record holds what the runtime was actually given. The test writes its own versions file in its temporary directory, a JSON object whose rauthy_image_id is sha256: followed by 64 hexadecimal characters of the test's making and whose postgres_image is a digest reference of the test's making, and runs the child as `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py --versions-file <that file>`. Every image ID and reference the stub answers for and every case asserts on is the one written in that file. The stub answers version, image inspect, the revision label or its absence, network create, run, exec pg_isready, port, stop, rm and network rm as the case under test directs. The port it reports belongs to a std::net::TcpListener the test runs on 127.0.0.1, which answers /auth/v1/health as the case directs and counts the requests it receives. The test reads the expected pin itself with git rev-parse HEAD:vendor/rauthy. The secret values it searches for SHALL be the ones the stub record shows the runtime received for POSTGRES_PASSWORD, PG_PASSWORD, ENC_KEYS, BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_PLAIN, HQL_SECRET_RAFT and HQL_SECRET_API, and never values the test or the script substitutes. The test SHALL search the child's complete stdout and stderr for each distinct value, both as written and as its lowercase hexadecimal. IF python3 or git is absent from the test's environment, THEN THE TEST SHALL fail naming the absent tool, and it SHALL NOT skip. THE TEST SHALL NOT start a real container, reach a real daemon, or open any port except its own listener. THE TEST SHALL NOT write a fixed credential, token or key value into the test source. THE TEST SHALL NOT be marked #[ignore]. THE TEST SHALL NOT write, create or delete anything under deploy/identity/.
acceptance: Case ready: the listener answers 200 with {"db_healthy":true,"cache_healthy":true}. The child exits 0, stdout holds one line beginning 'ready:', and the listener counted at least 1 request.
Case ready, secrets: the stub record yields exactly 5 distinct secret values, and the test asserts that count equals 5. The child's stdout and stderr contain each of the 5 values 0 times.
Search control: the same search function, run over the stub record's env-file text, finds each of the 5 values at least once, proving the search fires.

Case ready, cleanup: every name the stub record shows in a run --name or network create argument appears in a later rm or network rm argument. The count of names created equals the count removed, and every removed name begins lys-rauthy-ready-.
Case ready, no pull: the stub record holds 0 argv whose first argument is pull, and each of its 2 run argv carries --pull never.
Case no runtime: PATH holds only python3 and git. The child exits 1, stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: container_runtime_missing', and stdout holds no 'ready:' line.

Case no Rauthy image: stub image inspect fails for the Rauthy image ID recorded in the versions file the case supplies. The child exits 1, stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: image_missing' that contains 'rauthy', that image ID, and 'docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=' followed by the pin the test read and ' --load .'. That line contains 'pull' 0 times, and the stub record holds 0 run argv.

Case no PostgreSQL image: stub image inspect fails for the PostgreSQL reference. The child exits 1, stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: image_missing' that contains 'postgres' and 'pull', and the stub record holds 0 run argv.

Case revision differs: the stub reports the Rauthy image ID present, and its label is 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. The child exits 1, stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: rauthy_revision_mismatch', and the stub record holds 0 run argv.

Case revision absent: the stub reports no org.opencontainers.image.revision label. The child exits 1, stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: rauthy_revision_mismatch' that contains 'absent', the pin the test read, and 'docker buildx build --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=', and the stub record holds 0 run argv.

Case never ready: the listener answers 500 for every request. The child exits 1 and stderr holds a line beginning 'refused: readiness_timeout' that contains 'rauthy'. Every name the stub saw created was removed, and the 5 secret values occur 0 times in stdout and stderr.

The test file declares exactly 10 #[test] functions, one for each of the 10 cases above: ready; ready, secrets; ready, cleanup; ready, no pull; no runtime; no Rauthy image; no PostgreSQL image; revision differs; revision absent; never ready. The search control is not a #[test] of its own: it runs inside the ready, secrets test. cargo test --workspace --all-features reports each of the 10 as passed. After the test run, `git status --porcelain -- deploy/identity` prints the same lines as before it.

files_changed.note: An integration test (#![cfg(test)]) with 10 #[test] functions. Each runs `python3 scripts/identity-gates/rauthy_ready.py --versions-file <its own file>` from the repository root. PATH starts with a stub docker that records every argv and every --env-file's contents, and a loopback TcpListener the test owns answers /auth/v1/health and counts requests. It adds no dependency (serde_json is already a normal dependency and tempfile a dev-dependency).

The never-ready case waits out the script's 60-second bound.
